column4: These experiments were conducted by the USGS in a debris-flow flume near Blue River, Oregon.
Volumes from Table 1 of Iverson and George (2019). Talbe also contains more details about experiments (bulk densities, porosity, saturation)
Allstadt and others (2019) uses seismic data from some of these experiments.
Non-seismic sensor data from these experiments (basal stresses, flow thickness) is available at Iverson and Logan (2017)

Note that the highest amplitude signals on most of the seismic traces for these experiments come at the onset of the signal due to the gate latch opening and then the gates hitting the wall about a second later. The signal of the gate should be excluded from analysis.
Raw waveforms from closest broadband stations. Data was demeaned but no other processing was applied. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present.

Very high frequency (15+ Hz) ground velocity waveforms for station response from closest broadband stations. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Waveforms are corrected for station response after removing the mean. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Clipped waveforms have not been removed before station correction so check raw plots before interpreting high amplitude signals.
